author: Drew Miller
title: Teen victim of fatal e-bike crash identified as junior firefighter - NewsBreak
text:
By Drew Miller Jennifer Mobilia Brady Doran ,
1 days ago
UPDATE Sep. 22: The 17-year-old who died after his e-bike collided with a car has now been identified as a junior firefighter.
Erie County Deputy Coroner John Maloney said the 17-year-old Girard boy died Monday evening at UPMC Hamot of blunt force trauma and ruled the death as accidental.
A statement from the chief of the Dobler Hose Company in Girard identified the victim as Junior Firefighter Bryce Kaufmann and confirmed the accident happened as he was responding to an emergency call.
A 17-year-old is in critical condition after colliding with a car while riding his e-bike Sunday afternoon, according to Pennsylvania State Police in Girard.
Police said the crash happened around 2:13 Sunday afternoon at the intersection of West Lake Road and Culbertson Drive in Girard Township.
Police said the 17-year-old boy was heading south on Culbertson Drive and didn't stop at the stop sign and hit a sedan on its front right side, ejecting the teen from the bike.
The initial release from PSP Girard stated the teen had sustained fatal injuries; however, the Erie County Coroner's Office told us he has not been declared dead as of Monday morning and remains in critical condition at UPMC Hamot.
According to a statement from the Pennsylvania Office of the State Fire Commissioner, Governor Josh Shapiro has ordered Commonwealth and U.S. flags at all Commonwealth facilities to be flown at half-staff in Kaufmann's honor.
The statement added that flags will remain lowered to half-staff until the date of interment.
